title: Level-One Fock Space and Residue Crystals

items.title: The symmetric-group level-one residue and partition-label convention
items.statement: Fix finite e≥2 and charge0. English nodes(r,c) have residue c−r mod e, with the full independent-root affine datum already fixed. An e-regular partition has every positive-part multiplicity<e; an e-restricted partition has lambda_a−lambda_(a+1)<e for every a. Thus lambda restricted iff lambda-prime regular. The MODULAR/restricted signature lists corners top-to-bottom, cancels −+, takes good removable FIRST surviving− and cogood addable LAST surviving+. Crystal labels of the basic module here are restricted shapes. To make the ambient module comparison exact, define the Q(q)-linear isomorphism J:F_sym→F_QG by J M_lambda=|lambda-prime>. Define E_i^sym=J^-1 E_-i^QG J,F_i^sym=J^-1 F_-i^QG J,K_h^sym=J^-1 K_(tau h)^QG J, and psi_sym=J^-1 psi_QG J; J does not invert q. The standard chart is ⊕ A0 M_lambda. Its full crystal has ALL partitions; its empty component restricted shapes. Weight is Lambda0−Σ_i m_i(lambda)alpha_i; J applies tau:i→−i to weight. The conjugation map exchanges addable/removable node TYPES with themselves and negates residue, and is a map BETWEEN models, not the same-model sign/Mullineux involution. In characteristic p>0 with e=p prime, simple labels satisfy D^mu=D(mu-prime)⊗sgn; for Hecke algebras finite e is the quantum characteristic, not necessarily prime. The source boundary e=0 means no positive e with 1+xi+...+xi^(e−1)=0; colors are Z and every level-one partition is a crystal label. No finite affine datum is claimed there.
items.strategy: Compute c−r→r−c and m_i(lambda)=m_-i(lambda-prime). Adjacent differences count column multiplicities, proving restricted/regular equivalence with <e rather than an exactly-e exclusion. Linear transport defines a genuine full ambient quantum module, crystal lattice and bar, and its operators have the required reflected colors. Kleshchev complete §2.1 defines quantum characteristic; §3.4/Example3.2 gives the top-to-bottom −+ signature and restricted level-one labels. Remark5.5 gives the James simple-label/sign dictionary under its stated symmetric/Hecke regimes. This does not identify lower with upper or a linear J with the semilinear transpose occurring in an adjoint-bar formula. Same-model Mullineux is separately the supplier's universal diagram-reflection involution; restricted version is C M C^-1. All elementary transports are explicit and choice-free; source branching results remain with the actual modular suppliers.

items.title: Residue-node reading orders and the conjugation dictionary
items.statement: For distinct addable/removable corners of one residue i (finite e≥2), smaller row implies strictly larger column and strictly larger content. Hence top-to-bottom=DECREASING content=decreasing column; bottom-to-top=increasing content. A same-residue row or column cannot repeat. Conjugation sends a top-to-bottom i-corner list of lambda to the bottom-to-top (increasing content) −i-corner list of lambda-prime, preserving signs. Thus its modular −+ cancellations, FIRST− good deletion and LAST+ cogood addition agree exactly with the QG INCREASING-content −+ rule on lambda-prime. Equivalently reverse the latter list and use decreasing-content +− cancellation, LAST− deletion and FIRST+ addition. Both versions select the same actual nodes. They apply to all partitions as signatures; the basic graph restriction is imposed separately.
items.strategy: Let rows r<s. Boundary inequalities give c_r≥c_s: check removable/removable, addable/addable, addable/removable directly from weak row lengths; for removable/addable, the upper removable drop and lower addability give the same weak inequality. Equality is possible for mixed types, so the native general 'impossible' assertion was false. If a removable upper corner and an addable lower corner share a column, their rows must be adjacent at that column's boundary, hence their contents differ1; the reverse mixed orientation cannot share a column. Equal-row mixed corners also differ1 in content. Same-residue e≥2 excludes these exceptions. Strict columns and r<s imply strictly DECREASING content. Conjugating exchanges rows/columns and negates content, yielding the stated order reversal. Stack reduction of −+ is uniquely determined: scan with a minus stack, cancel each plus with the last unmatched minus; reversing the word yields +− with first/last extrema reversed. Therefore the surviving-node bijection and selected-node identities are exact, not only an abstract isomorphism. This is the full elementary proof supplementing Fayers §4, whose text records the conventions but omits proofs.

items.title: The QG Fock-crystal arrows are the modular good-node operators
items.statement: Conjugation C sends the restricted/modular crystal on restricted lambda onto the EMPTY COMPONENT of the QG full partition Fock crystal, with colors negated: C tilde-e_i lambda=tilde-e_-i^QG C lambda and C tilde-f_i lambda=tilde-f_-i^QG C lambda, including zero values. Epsilon_i/phi_i are the numbers of surviving−/+, and weight transforms by tau. With the explicitly transported full module F_sym the modular signatures give its Kashiwara operators on ALL partitions, whose restricted subset is its basic component. Good is removable (tilde-e), cogood addable (tilde-f) in BOTH conventions; there is no opposite naming-polarity dictionary. Ordinary Chevalley coefficients, especially negative powers, do not define these arrows.
items.strategy: Apply the supplier order lemma: the modular top-to-bottom word on lambda is exactly the QG increasing-content word on lambda-prime at−i, with identical −+ cancellations and identical FIRST−/LAST+ extrema. Node removal/addition commutes with transpose, so each formula and its zero condition follows. The actual QG fixed-residue cube theorem proves lattice stability and the signature rule on crystal residues; on raw vectors the selected partition formulas are congruences modulo q times the A0 partition lattice, without a minimum-Chevalley-exponent argument. The empty-component theorem proves the image of restricted shapes is exactly the regular/basic component; full Fock is larger. Weight and epsilon/phi follow the same bijection. Kleshchev §3.4 and the established modular good-node suppliers supply the restricted reading and inverse property. Native recorded contradictions are resolved at the supplier, not deferred to Step3.

items.title: The restricted-partition component is the basic crystal in the symmetric-group convention
items.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice exactly through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]], which uses it to split an integrable module with a crystal basis into highest-weight components; the identification of the empty component with the $e$-restricted partitions themselves is choice-free (Kleshchev Theorem 8.2(ii) with Example 3.2(i) and Fayers' restricted model are direct constructions of the crystal on that vertex set). The choice-free alternative is recorded in the strategy.
items.statement: For finite e≥2 the empty component of F_sym is exactly the e-restricted partitions, with modular good deletions/cogood additions and wt(lambda)=Lambda0−Σ m_i alpha_i. It is B(Lambda0), every restricted shape is reached from empty, and epsilon/phi count normal/conormal nodes. The entire F_sym has ALL partitions and is reducible, with the transported full p(k) highest-module decomposition; its other vertices are the nonrestricted shapes. In the symmetric-group regime of algebraically closed characteristic p>0 and xi=1, e=p is PRIME: restricted labels lambda correspond to James simples D^(lambda-prime)=D(lambda)⊗sgn, and if epsilon_i(lambda)>0 then soc E_-i D^(lambda-prime)=D^((tilde-e_i lambda)-prime). The standard E_-i is the residue functor after sign twist. General finite-e Hecke crystal labels remain valid but are not called symmetric-group modules of 'characteristic e'. At quantum characteristic e=0 (colors Z), every level-one partition is in the empty sl_infinity crystal; there are no same-content corner cancellations, and no finite-affine assertion is made.
items.strategy: Apply J/C with color reflection to the proved full QG crystal and its exact regular empty component. Restricted iff conjugate regular proves containment, converse reachability and the unique top. Transfer the full module decomposition through the field isomorphism; this is not an integral splitting claim. The established modular suppliers identify normal/conormal counts and restriction socle. In source Kleshchev §2.1 e is quantum characteristic; §3.4/Example3.2(i),(ii) gives labels and the e0 boundary, Theorem8.2(ii) gives B(Lambda0), and Theorem7.4(i), not Theorem11.6(i), gives the simple socle. Remark5.5 under xi=1 supplies the sign/transposed James labels. Sign twist negates Jucys-Murphy residue, so E_-i(D(lambda)⊗sgn)=E_iD(lambda)⊗sgn and its simple socle gives the displayed label. This consumes the actual modular branching theorem; the stronger normal multiplicities stay with batch22. At e0, distinct corners have distinct integer contents, so no cancellation; any removable corner can be removed and every shape is reached, giving the stated elementary graph boundary. Choice assumptions of the full field decomposition are inherited explicitly, not hidden in the finite signature comparison.

items.title: Level-one global-basis transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention
items.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] (and hence through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]) for the decomposition of the Fock space into highest-weight components; the definition of the polynomials themselves and the pairing are choice-free. Consumers must carry the same assumption while it is used.
items.statement:
Work in the linear symmetric-group model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: the
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$-linear isomorphism $J M_\mu = |\mu'\rangle$, the transported
action, bar and $A_0$ standard chart $(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$, and the weight
$\operatorname{wt}(M_\mu) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\mu)\alpha_i$, with
$A = \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$.

**The basic module and its lower basis.** Let
$M_{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0) = J^{-1}M_{\mathrm{QG}}$ be the
transported highest-weight module of the vacuum; by
[[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
its crystal is the $e$-restricted component and its labels are the $e$-restricted
partitions. For an $e$-restricted $\lambda$ define
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) := J^{-1}G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda'),$$
where $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)$ is the lower global (canonical) basis element of
the Fock space at the standard vector $|\mu\rangle$
([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).
Then $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) \equiv M_\lambda \bmod q\,(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$
and the family $\{G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)\}$ is the transported lower global
basis of $M_{\mathrm{sym}}$, indexed by the restricted labels. Define the
**level-one transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention** by the
finite weightwise expansion
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) = \sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\, M_\mu ,$$
the sum being over the partitions $\mu$ of the weight of $\lambda$.

**Ambient polarization and ambient upper coordinates.** Define the ambient
polarization by $B(M_\mu,M_\nu) = \delta_{\mu\nu}$ on the standard basis, a
symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on each finite weight space. Fix a weight
$w$ and let $V_w$ be the (finite-dimensional) weight space of
$F_{\mathrm{sym}}$; let $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ be the matrix with columns the
coordinate vectors of $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)$ for the finitely many
$e$-restricted $\lambda$ of weight $w$, and rows the **standard** shapes
$M_\mu$, $\mu$ of weight $w$; let
$$H := D_{\mathrm{rect}}^{\mathsf{t}}\, D_{\mathrm{rect}} , \qquad G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda) := \sum_\mu \bigl(D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1}\bigr)_{(\mu,\lambda)}\, M_\mu^* ,$$
where $M_\mu^*$ denotes the ambient orthonormal dual frame of the standard
basis. The $G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda)$ are the **ambient upper coordinates**
of the basic module: they are the unique elements of the basic subspace
$(M_{\mathrm{sym}})_w\subseteq V_w$ characterized weightwise by $B(G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda), G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda')) = \delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$,
and are viewed in the ambient standard frame; adding a vector of the
$B$-orthogonal complement in $V_w$ gives other ambient representatives with
the same pairings. The coefficients
$e_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q) := (D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1})_{(\mu,\lambda)}$ lie in
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$ but need not be Laurent integral or polynomial. They are
coordinates in the ambient space and not a "standard basis of the basic
module"; the exact integral upper basis is the transported upper global basis of
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]], whose
restricted graded $A$-dual lattice is free weightwise and perfectly paired with
the basic lower $A$-span, while no lower-$A$ selfduality, no $A$-unit $H$ and no
full algebraic duality in infinite rank is implied. The restriction of $B$ to the basic module equals the normalized transported
contravariant form (proved in step 4.2), so these are the same upper vectors
viewed in the ambient standard frame and in their own integral dual lattice.
Upper bar is the adjoint bar
$\psi^\vee$ with its own dual infinity chart and weighted upper operators, not
the ordinary lower bar.

**The full ambient case.** On the whole Fock space the analogous matrix
$D_{\mathrm{full}}$, with columns the $G(\mu)$ over all partitions and rows the
standard shapes, is unitriangular (diagonal $1$, in $q\mathbb{Z}[q]$ below the
diagonal), and the dual matrix with respect to $B$ is
$$D_{\mathrm{full}}^{-\mathsf{t}},$$
which is Laurent integral because the inverse of a unitriangular matrix with
entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ has entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$.

**A worked instance.** At $e = 2$ the restricted shape $\lambda = (1,1)$ has
$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(1,1) = M_{1,1} + q\,M_{2}$, so $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ has the
single column $(q,1)^{\mathsf{t}}$, $H = 1 + q^2$, and
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(1,1) = \frac{M_{1,1}^* + q\,M_2^*}{1+q^2} = \frac{M_{1,1} + q\,M_2}{1+q^2},$$
an explicit ambient coordinate that is rational but not Laurent integral:
$1 + q^2$ is not a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$. No specialization of the $d$
to decomposition numbers of Hecke algebras is asserted here without the
separate correct Hecke parameter hypotheses.
items.strategy: Transport the lower Fock basis by the linear transpose-label map J, preserving q; obtain the exact coefficient identity, symmetric dominance direction, same-core and full reflected-weight support. Work weightwise with the rectangular lower-column matrix D and ambient orthonormal form. D(0) has distinct coordinate columns, so H=D^tD satisfies H(0)=I and is field invertible; DH^-1 gives the unique upper vectors inside the basic subspace, with whole-ambient representatives differing by its orthogonal complement. Compute the e=2 rational coordinates and the full ambient transpose-inverse matrix separately. The finite node-count identity Nright+Nleft=N(lambda)-1 proves sigma-adjointness of the orthonormal form; normalized highest-weight form uniqueness identifies its basic restriction with the transported QG form. Thus these upper vectors form the restricted integral dual basis with perfect pairing, while rational standard coordinates imply neither lower-A selfduality nor an A-unit Gram matrix. Transport the exact adjoint upper bar, dual charts and weighted operators; preserve all linear/semilinear and Hecke-parameter boundaries.

title: Level-One Fock Space and Residue Crystals — Examples

items.title: The Fock E- and F-actions on the shape (2,1) at e = 3
items.statement: At e3 the QG standard vector |21> has F0=|22>,F1=q^-1|211>,F2=|31>; E0=0,E1=q^-1|11>,E2=|2>. The transported symmetric standard vector M21 has F0_sym=M22,F1_sym=M211,F2_sym=q^-1 M31; E0_sym=0,E1_sym=M11,E2_sym=q^-1 M2, since J transposes outputs AND reflects colors. The QG normalized crystal residue at21 has f0→22,f1→211,e1→11, and f2=e2=0. In the restricted symmetric model it instead has f0→22,f2→31,e2→2, and f1=e1=0. Raw21 IS a representative of its crystal residue in each model; an ordinary q^-1F coefficient does not refute that fact. Its Chevalley action is not its normalized Kashiwara action.
items.strategy: QG corners have addable(1,3)res2,(2,2)res0,(3,1)res1 and removable(1,2)res1,(2,1)res2. For F1 the bottom addition sees one removable1 on its right, exponent−1. E1 computes N_l on the smaller11, giving1 and coefficientq^-1; E2 on smaller2 gives0. Other coefficients are1. In decreasing-content QG order the color1 word−+ survives, selecting e at the top− and f at the bottom+; color2 word+− cancels, so both normalized arrows vanish although its ordinary F2/E2 are nonzero. The fixed-residue finite tensor cube proves this distinction at the actual raw A0 chart, not through invented global corrections. Apply J^-1 and negate color to the module table: QG211 transposes31 and QG31 transposes211; for i_sym1 use i_QG2, giving M211, and for i_sym2 use i_QG1, givingq^-1M31. The signature lemma gives the stated restricted crystal table. Leclerc Exercise15 is a calibration of the same SMALLER-diagram exponent convention, not this printed example.

items.title: The charge-zero level-one crystal through rank four at e = 3
items.statement: At $e=3$, charge $\Lambda_0$, in the symmetric-group convention, the empty component through rank four has exactly the following vertices, one row per rank: rank $0$: $\varnothing$; rank $1$: $(1)$; rank $2$: $(2)$ and $(1,1)$; rank $3$: $(2,1)$ and $(1,1,1)$; rank $4$: $(3,1)$, $(2,2)$, $(2,1,1)$ and $(1,1,1,1)$. These are exactly the $3$-restricted partitions of each size ($1,1,2,2,4$ of them). The cogood-addition arrows staying within ranks0–4 are: $\varnothing\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1)$; $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2)$, $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(1,1)$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(2,1)$; $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(1,1,1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(2,2)$, $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$; $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1,1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2,1,1)$; All other additions from ranks0–3 vanish; additions from rank4 leaving the displayed window are omitted, not declared zero. The good-deletion arrows into the listed ranks are: $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}\varnothing$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1)$, $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1)$; $(2,2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(2,1)$, $(3,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2,1)$, $(2,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(1,1,1)$. In particular $(2,1)$ has no arrow of residue $1$ in either direction, and $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$ is the arrow whose conjugate is the QG-6 Fock arrow $\tilde f_1$ from $(2,1)$ to $(2,1,1)$.
items.strategy: Finite verification by the reduced $i$-signature, hand-checkable at every vertex. Compute for each listed partition and each $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ the residues $c-r$, list the addable and removable $i$-nodes from top to bottom, cancel $-$ above $+$ pairs and read the topmost surviving $-$ and the bottommost surviving $+$. For example at $(1,1)$ and $i=1$ the two addable nodes $(1,2)$ and $(3,1)$ both survive, giving $\tilde f_1(1,1)=(1,1,1)$; at $(2,1)$ and $i=1$ the removable node $(1,2)$ lies above the addable node $(3,1)$ and the pair cancels, so $\varepsilon_1=\varphi_1=0$ and both arrows vanish; at $(2,1)$ and $i=2$ the addable node $(1,3)$ lies above the removable node $(2,1)$, the word $+-$ does not cancel, and $\tilde f_2(2,1)=(3,1)$, $\tilde e_2(2,1)=(2)$. Residue labels are $c-r$ as fixed in the convention item. The list of $3$-restricted partitions is the direct check of $\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<3$; the count $1,1,2,2,4$ matches the multiplicity of $V(\Lambda_0)$ (Leclerc, *Fock space representations of U_q(sl_n^)*, sec. 3.14, printed pp. 25-26, where the $n$-regular labels give the basic representation; the restricted reading is the transpose/sign dictionary of the convention item). No module theory is used beyond the vertex list of [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]. The rank4 outgoing boundary is deliberately omitted; completeness/zero claims concern only ranks0–3. This derived finite signature calculation is not a claimed printed native source example.

items.title: The full Fock space is not automatically the irreducible basic module
items.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; the exhibited non-containment facts themselves are finite checks.
items.statement: At e3 the entire F_sym is strictly larger than its cyclic basic module. The shape4 is not3-restricted since4−0≥3; its conjugate is1111 (NOT111), which is not3-regular since part1 has multiplicity4≥3. Both raw M4 in F_sym and |1111> in F_QG are nonzero and are OUTSIDE their respective field basic modules, and their ambient lower global lifts are outside too. The full signature rule remains meaningful on these shapes in the full Fock crystal; for example restricted-model e0(4)=3 is an edge of another component, not a route into the empty component. Modular/basic signature statements restricted to restricted labels do not apply to4 as a basic label.
items.strategy: Restricted/regular and transposed size checks are immediate. To prove actual vector exclusion rather than graph-only exclusion, apply the actual top-isotypic crystal-lattice splitting theorem to F_QG at its maximal one-dimensional top Lambda0: F0_QG∩V(Lambda0) is the canonical lower lattice and its residue basis exactly the regular empty component. If raw1111 were in this module, its nonzero nonregular residue would lie in that component's span, contradicting residue-basis splitting. Its ambient lower lift has the same residue and is also excluded. Transport by the genuine field and chart isomorphism J gives M4 and its lift. At4, the sole removable0 node is(1,4), so the full restricted signature yields e0→3; neither shape is in the restricted empty component (3−0≥3), hence this edge is compatible with the full decomposable crystal. This corrects the native assertion that the signature had no ambient crystal meaning, while preserving the modular restricted-vertex hypothesis and the strongest field-vector boundary.
